title: Iterative control-group scaling and rollback sentinel for multi-arm experiments
creator: Sofia Martens
description: Establish an iterative approach to ramping control-group sizes across multi-arm experiments and implement a composite 'rollback sentinel' that triggers automated or manual rollback when a set of leading indicators cross defined thresholds. Focus is on production inferencing experiments (routing policies, quantization toggles, cache policies) where small regressions compound system cost or user experience.
acceptance_criteria: A documented ramp schedule that defines sample-size stages, stabilization windows, and statistical tests for multi-arm experiments
Rollback sentinel defined as a composable, testable rule set using signal weights (latency p95, error rate, semantic-quality regression signal) and live in monitoring with alerting hooks
Playbook for automated rollback and operator escalation verified in a dry run with synthetic traffic
Dashboards show per-arm and aggregated sentinel score; historical backfill for previous 90 days available for postmortem
Dependencies (ENG and DS PRs) resolved and integration tests pass in staging
success_metrics: Reduction in mean time to detect harmful regressions from rollouts by >= 40%
Zero customer-facing incidents caused by experiment rollouts in first 3 months after rollout
At least one cross-functional canary executed using the new ramp schedule and sentinel during cycle-10
instrumentation_checklist: Per-request routing tag (experiment_arm, cohort_id, sampling_stage) emitted to tracing
Token-level latency histogram and p95/p99 metrics per arm
Semantic-quality evaulation hooks: batch async evals for a seeded prompt set and daily aggregate score
KV-cache hit rate and batch sizes instrumented per-arm
Error taxonomy counters (model-timeouts, inference-errors, downstream-io) segregated by arm
Sentinel score computation exported as a metric for SLOs and alerting
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (shadow): 0% traffic; validate instrumentation and cost estimates against shadow logs (2 days)
Stage 1 (micro-ramp): assign 0.5% control and 0.5% treatment traffic for 24h, run non-parametric check for distribution shift
Stage 2 (small): increase to 2% per-arm for 48h, evaluate sentinel score and semantic-quality baseline
Stage 3 (medium): 10% per-arm for 72h, run full statistical tests and cost sensitivity analysis
Stage 4 (gradual): expand in multiples (25%, 50%) with 24–72h stabilization windows before each step
Final: full commit only after pass of all sentinel thresholds and post-rollout smoke tests
risk_mitigation: Conservative time windows for each ramp stage to avoid exposure to diurnal variability
Isolation of experiment traffic by customer segment to limit business-critical impact
Pre-registered fallback variants: compatible lower-cost model and regional fallback
Quota guardrails to limit spend during unexpected token-rate increases
Runbook entry prepared with triage steps and rollback triggers mapped to exact metric deltas
monitoring_playbook: Sentinel alert severity mapping: warning (investigate) vs critical (auto-rollback)
On-call rotations for experiments week: include PM + ENG + DS in first 6 hours of each stage
Post-incident checklist: collect trace ids, sample requests, KV cache snapshots, and seeded prompt evals
Escalation ladder: on-call -> experiment lead -> Head of Product Operations -> CTO
